newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas introduced Lousewies van der Laan, the new spokeswoman for Commissioner Hans van den Broek. Formerly in van den Broek's cabinet, she replaces Nicolaas Wegter, who will head the information bureau of the Commission representation in The Hague.

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida briefed on the informal Development Council. The ministers discussed ways to make the EU's other policies coherent with its development policy, preventing conflicts in Africa, a green paper on relations with African, Caribbean and Pacific countries, and United Nations reform.

Responding to questions about EU policy toward Albania, van der Laan said a joint Commission-EU presidency mission there on Friday had confirmed that the situation was explosive. She said the Commission wanted all parties, including the opposition, to be calm and abstain from using the situation for political gain. Albania now seemed ready to accept technical assistance that the EU had been offering since October to resolve the problem of the collapse of the pyramid schemes, she said.

Van der Laan said the Commission would work with the IMF and World Bank to provide the assistance and hoped the new Albanian government would confirm the decision to accept it. She said an EU working group would likely meet later this week to see if the EU needed to take steps beyond those agreed by the General Affairs Council last week.

Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan said Renault's decision to close its Belgian plant was covered by two EU directives -- one on collective redundancies and another on consulting European Works Councils. However, if Renault has violated either directive it is up to national courts to act, not the Commission, she said.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/170: The Commission authorises the acquisition of Air Liberte by British Airways.
- IP/97/171: "Second chance" schools: after France (Marseille), now Spain, Italy, Greece, Portugal and Finland are following.
